# PRV-RGT-01

**Does a scenario show how one person's data is found, exported, corrected or erased, across every store that holds it?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [Privacy by design](privacy.md) 0.1.0 |
| Area | RGT: Rights of the people the data is about |
| Default severity | major |
| Decided by | A tool checks presence; a reviewer judges |
| Reads | `scenarios.name`, `scenarios.stimulus` |

## Why it matters

A right of access or erasure the design cannot carry out is a breach waiting for its first request. A scenario makes the design say where the data is and how it is reached, including copies in caches, logs, indexes and model memory.

## Rule

At least one scenario's name or stimulus speaks of access, export, rectification, erasure or deletion of a person's data; a reviewer judges whether it reaches every store.

## Check

The tool applies this rule as written:

```yaml
- for_each: scenarios
  where:
    .:
      matches: >-
        eras|delet|subject access|export|rectif|right to be forgotten|data
        subject
  count:
    min: 1
  message: >-
    no scenario shows how a person's data is found, exported, corrected or
    erased
```

## Sources

- Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Articles 15 to 20, the rights of the data subject. (`gdpr-15-20`)
- ISO/IEC 29100, Information technology, Security techniques, Privacy framework. (`iso-29100`)
